title: Owning a Drawing Package End to End
objective: Move from task execution to controlled ownership of a small electrical drawing package from brief through coordination, checking, revision and issue.

learn.heading: What senior designers should understand
bullets: Package ownership begins with inputs, scope, deliverables, interfaces and approval boundaries.
A drawing register and revision strategy make package status visible.
Design decisions should be traceable to inputs, calculations, standards or approved engineering direction.
Coordination and checking are planned activities, not a final formatting step.
A senior designer knows when to decide, when to verify and when to escalate.
learn.takeaway: Ownership is demonstrated by controlling the workflow and interfaces, not simply by producing drawings quickly.

apply.scenario: You are responsible for a fictional six-sheet LV pump-station electrical package containing an SLD, panel GA, cable schedule, earthing layout, equipment layout and notes sheet.
tasks: Create a drawing register showing sheet purpose, status, revision and dependencies.
Build an input/interface register covering civil, mechanical, vendor and electrical inputs.
Define a practical checking sequence before issue.
Identify five package risks and assign an action or escalation route to each.
Write an issue-readiness checklist that another designer could execute.
apply.deliverable: A sanitized drawing register, interface/risk register and issue-readiness checklist.

a: Completing the largest number of sheets personally.
Controlling scope, inputs, interfaces, revisions, checks and issue readiness.
questions.why: Ownership is about controlled delivery and coordination.

questions.q: An upstream vendor drawing changes after your package check. What should you do?
a: Ignore it if your sheets were already checked.
Assess affected interfaces, update the change/revision trail and repeat relevant checks.
questions.why: Changes must be assessed for downstream impact.

questions.q: What should a risk register do?
a: Make risks, impacts, actions, owners and escalation visible.
questions.why: A useful risk register drives controlled action and escalation.

check.passRule: Select the strongest response and be able to explain the ownership principle behind it.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized package register, interface register or issue-readiness checklist demonstrating end-to-end ownership.

integration.home: Recommend Week 8 and show package ownership as the latest milestone.
integration.journal: Reflect on which parts of package ownership you can perform independently and which still require engineering direction.
integration.portfolio: Add the package-control artefact as evidence of end-to-end ownership.
